steps: Explored the target homepage and identified the search parameter reflects user input
Identified the Content-Security-Policy header with report-uri directive containing a controllable token parameter
Crafted CSP bypass by injecting ;script-src-elem 'unsafe-inline' into the token parameter
Combined the CSP bypass with a reflected <script>alert(1)</script> payload in the search parameter
Verified lab solved by confirming 'Congratulations' text on the homepage
evidence: CSP after injection: default-src 'self'; object-src 'none';script-src 'self'; style-src 'self'; report-uri /csp-report?token=;script-src-elem 'unsafe-inline'
Script tag reflected in response body: <script>alert(1)</script>
Homepage contains 'Congratulations' text confirming lab is solved
comments: The CSP bypass leverages Chrome's script-src-elem directive which takes precedence over script-src for inline script elements. By injecting this directive via the controllable token parameter in report-uri, the inline script execution restriction is bypassed.
